We need to create test class, with @Test methods. Use jsoup library to create org.jsoup.nodes.Document with elements, attributes, namespaces, text nodes, comments, data nodes. Then call W3CDom.fromJsoup and verify resulting W3C Document structure: element names, namespace URIs, attributes, text nodes, comment nodes.

Also test copyAttributes filters invalid attribute names.

We need to access copyAttributes and updateNamespaces maybe via reflection because they are private. But we can test behavior indirectly via conversion.

Test cases:

1. Simple element without namespaces: <html><body>Hello</body></html>. Convert and verify root element name "html", child "body", text node "Hello". Also ensure document URI set when location non-blank.

2. Namespace handling: create element with xmlns attribute and prefixed child. Example: <root xmlns="http://default" xmlns:ns="http://ns"><ns:child attr="val">Text</ns:child></root>. Convert and verify that child element has namespace URI "http://ns". Also default namespace for root.

3. Attribute name sanitization: include attribute with invalid characters, e.g., "data-!bad" should be sanitized (non-matching chars removed) then check if resulting attribute key matches regex. Actually copyAttributes strips characters not allowed and then checks matches pattern; if after removal matches, it will be set. So we can test attribute with illegal chars that become valid after removal, and attribute that becomes invalid and thus not set.

4. Comment and DataNode handling: add comment node and data node and verify they appear as Comment and Text nodes.

5. asString: after conversion, call asString and ensure string contains expected XML fragments (e.g., root start tag, namespaces). Also test that IllegalStateException is thrown when transformer fails? Hard to simulate; we can just test normal case.

6. Test that fromJsoup throws IllegalStateException when DocumentBuilderFactory fails? Hard to simulate; maybe we can pass null to fromJsoup expecting NullPointerException due to Validate.notNull (but Validate not defined here; maybe internal). But we can test that passing null throws NullPointerException (or maybe IllegalArgumentException). We'll just test that.
